summary:
# BOOK 1 of 2: PASSING BY (Maurice Baring, 1921)

Format: diary entries of Godfrey Mellor (Gray's Inn, Foreign Office-type office, Lord Ayton's junior clerk, later "Mellor"), letters from Guy Cunninghame to cousin Mrs Elsie Caryl (Paris-based, husband Jack, later Copenhagen), and a few letters from others. Dates run Dec 1908 to Aug 1912.

## Core cast
- **Godfrey Mellor**: diarist, silent, Balliol, Gray's Inn office, reads Jane Eyre, aunt Ruth & uncle Arthur (Eccleston Square), aunt Lady Mellor, Lady Arthur Mellor is his aunt. Friend Alfred Riley (converts to Catholicism; Liverpool/Shelborough professor, editing Propertius). Friend Solway (pianist, Woking cottage). Hope (playwright). Tuke (A.'s secretary).
- **Lord Ayton ("A.", George Ayton)**: new Parliamentary Under-Secretary (Feb 1909); yachtsman; sister **Mrs Campion** (widow, house Wraxted Priory, Oxfordshire; later Pont Street); Littlehampton house, yacht (cutter). Falls in love with Mrs Housman. Appendicitis June 1910 (Welbeck Street nursing home). Refused Madras governorship. Dines with Lady Jarvis, Aunt Ruth.
- **Guy Cunninghame**: Ayton's unpaid Private Secretary, well-dressed, affable, Halkin Street flat; writes to cousin Mrs Caryl (Elsie) about everything. Later goes to Copenhagen (Caryls get Copenhagen posting). Cousin Freda Macdonald; Edith (sister) Mrs Howard? (Edith is a relative; Mrs Howard is Cunninghame's sister, Chester Street).
- **Mrs Clare Housman** (Clare): portrait by Walter Bell (New Gallery, later sold/bought); Canadian/Irish-born (actually raised in French-Canadian convent, Irish per Lady Jarvis); sings (Schubert, Schumann, Winterreise); devout Catholic; marries Albert Housman; in 1910 goes to Florence, Villa Fersen (Bellosguardo); later Cornwall (Grey Farm, Carbis Bay); enters Convent of the Presentation (Feb 1912, letter to Mellor). Earlier took Mellor to Vernon? (no).
- **Albert ("Bert") Housman**: wealthy stockjobber, firm Housman & Smith; partner Carrington-Smith; Campden Hill house; Staines (Thames villa); Oakley near Hendon (1910-11); "Ha! ha! ha!" laugh; unfaithful with Celia Russell, Mrs Rachel Park (ex-singer, Rose Sinclair), Mrs Fairburn (Florence, Easter 1911); has heart attack and dies at Oakley, Dec 1910 (Thursday 22 Dec, from letter read by Mellor). Baptized Catholic but agnostic.
- **Miss Sarah Housman** (Albert's sister): pianist, large, yellow satin, emerald ear-rings.
- **Lady Jarvis**: Rosedale (Surrey house, transplanted Tudor), Mansfield Street; intelligent, witty; close to Mrs Housman; knows A.'s love.
- **Mrs Shamier (Louise)** and **Mr Shamier MP** (cricket Blue; Upper Brook Street); Louise loves Lavroff (Russian philosopher) and leaves Shamier to go to Italy then Russia.
- **Lavinia Wray** (Miss Wray): A.'s possible match; refused Ralph Logan; goes to nursing.
- **Eileen Hope**: singer, Carrington-Smith's divorce scandal (Mrs Carrington-Smith got divorce Oct 1909).
- **Solway, Esther Lake, Miss Hope, Miss Bowden** (violinist), **Raphael Luc** (French singer), **Jane Vaughan**.
- **Father Stanway**: Carbis Bay priest, gives Mellor advice on nuns; Thomas à Kempis quotes.
- **Barnes** (F.O. gossip), **Ashfield** (American), **Miss Audrey Bax**.
- **General York and Mrs York** (Carbis Bay; Indian servant).
- **Lady Maria Lyneham**; **Mr Eugene Lowe** (Florence flat); **Mr Harold Jefferson** (American yachtsman); **Jimmy Randall** (city friend, Mrs Park, Housman's ally).
- Others: Admiral Bowes, Colonel Hamley, Grayson, Mr & Mrs Baines (Mrs Baines once "taken for Sarah Bernhardt"), Mrs Carrington-Smith (Kate in Henry James's Wings of the Dove, "Reform Kleid"), Princesse de Carignan, Mrs Campion's governess Fräulein Brandes, Mrs Howard (Cunninghame's sister), Edmund & Gertrude Anstruther (Buenos Aires; Edmund goes to Berne), Mrs de la Poer, Mrs Legget.

## Key events in order
- Dec 1908: Housmans leave for Egypt; Mellor's Christmas with Aunt Ruth.
- Feb 9 1909: Housmans return to Campden Hill house. Feb 15: house-warming; Mrs Housman's "passing by" remark ("people who are just passing by"); Solway plays; Lord Ayton (Cunninghame arrives Feb 17). Ayton new chief.
- Mrs Housman visits office re brother-in-law's billet; Cunninghame recognises her from Bell's picture (sold at Altheim's, NY).
- Mar 1909: Mellor dines with Housmans; Mrs Housman sings. Mellor dines with Cunninghame (Mrs Shamier "the love").
- Apr 1909: Mellor at Florence: Villa Fersen, Bellosguardo. Ayton & Mrs Campion arrive Easter Sunday (Apr 4). Mrs Housman sings "Passing By" (Edward Purcell's tune; words from Ford's Music of Sundry Kinds, 1607) for Countess Alberti; A. asks for it twice.
- Apr 1909: Cunninghame at Mentone; Monte Carlo; Celia Russell with Housman.
- May 1909: Cunninghame dinner at Carlton; Housman's dinner Campden Hill (Walter Bell picture; Snake Picture by "Mucius of Munich"). Cunninghame at Opera box with Housmans (Bohème). Staines weekend: Lady Jarvis reveals Housman unfaithful, Ayton in love with Clare.
- May 1909: Mellor & Riley: Riley thinking of becoming Catholic; Mellor & Mrs Housman talk of "Grace"; "The nursery anti-Catholic tradition".
- June 1909: Rosedale party; Ayton: "Passing By" song; Mrs Housman to Cornwall (Grey Farm, Carbis Bay, July–Sept 1909 summer).
- Aug 1909: Cornwall (Grey Farm, Carbis Bay): Mellor, Cunninghame, Lady Jarvis, Ayton's yacht; Mrs Carrington-Smith divorce; Cunninghame realises Ayton loves Clare. Father Stanway's views. Riley received into Catholic church (Brompton Oratory; Father X.). York & Mrs York.
- Sept 1909: Mellor with Miss Housman bridge; Mrs Baines & Mr Baines visit; "The Only Way."
- Oct 1909: Oxfordshire (Wraxted Priory, Mrs Campion); Mellor & Miss Wray; Oct 15 Mrs Carrington-Smith divorce granted; Rachel Park scene at Campden Hill dinner (Cunninghame letter). Mellor's Nov 1909: Ayton "hates official life".
- Dec 1909: Mrs Housman goes to Florence for winter; Housman's Mrs Park affair; Cornwall; Ayton at Florence Christmas.
- Jan 1910: Cunninghame at Rosedale; Mrs Housman returns to London Feb 1910; Riley and Mellor discuss Confession (Feb 16, "the Church is not an air cushion but a rock"). Mrs Housman: "Faith is a gift... invisible rope—Grace".
- Mar 1910: Florence Easter; Mrs Fairburn (Housman's new mistress). Mellor leaves Florence Apr 2.
- Apr–May 1910: Housman's Hendon house (Oakley later); Mrs Shamier leaves husband May 1910; Sir Henry St Clair (Ayton's godfather) and Madras offer refused (May).
- May 1910: Ayton/Riley/Lady Jarvis; Gertrude Anstruther's gossip.
- June 1910: Ayton's appendicitis (June 6); Mrs Housman visits him at Welbeck Street June 1910; Mellor dines with Caryls June 20.
- Summer 1910: Cornwall again (Grey Farm) July 30–Sept; Father Stanway; O. Henry readings; Mrs Housman on Les Misérables ("Ne craignons jamais les voleurs..." passage); Ayton sails; Mellor visits Oratory Oct 5, 1910 for Cunninghame's friend (married woman seeking annulment); Priest advises no.
- Oct 1910: Mrs Housman goes to Florence; Housman's Hendon house.
- Dec 22 1910: Housman's death at Oakley (heart attack) after reading a letter (from Clare) and tearing it; Mrs Housman at Garland's Hotel; Mellor misdirects a telegram ("Albert dangerously ill. Fear worst. Cannot come. Clare.") — Mellor opened and forwarded it to Hôtel Meurice.
- Feb 28 1911: Mrs Housman to be a nun (Convent of the Presentation). Mar 4: Mellor consults Father Stanway (Kensington Gardens); Stanway: "a vocation was a categorical imperative"; "the pendulum swings back"; quote "In la sua volontate e nostra pace."
- Aug 19 1911: Lady Jarvis: Mrs Housman took the white veil; irrevocable. Mellor, Cunninghame at Rosedale.
- Aug 26 1911: Mellor at Carbis Bay Hotel; Thomas à Kempis quotes ("By so much the more does a man draw nigh to God..." and "Whosoever is not ready to suffer all things..."). Aug 28 1911: Mellor resolves to give up diary.

Note on dates: entries are as in text; some dates the diary gives out of sequence (e.g., "Tuesday, June 12th" after June 13). Final entries 1911.

## Diary and letter structure
Diary entries named "From the Diary of Godfrey Mellor"; letters "Letter from Guy Cunninghame to Mrs Caryl." Letters signed "G." or "Yrs." Letters from Cunninghame include Edith (family), Worsel (country house), Edith's (family visit), Edith in Ireland (Shamiers lodge).

Key quotes:
- "passing by" (Mrs Housman, Feb 1909)
- "Clare, Clare, guests" (Housman shouting)
- "Ha! ha! ha!" (Housman)
- "Faith is a gift... pulled over by an invisible rope—what we call Grace"
- "Madam, you are here not from love of virtue, but from fear of vice" (Johnson, quoted by Cunninghame)
- "the Church is not an air cushion but a rock" (Riley)
- "Once the priests get hold of someone they will never let them go" (George Ayton quoted by Cunninghame)

# BOOK 2 of 2: DORCAS DENE, DETECTIVE (George R. Sims, Gutenberg 77243)

Narrator: "Mr Saxon," a dramatist and Dorcas's "assistant." Dorcas Dene (née Dorcas Lester; father an artist who died, mother Mrs Lester, stage name Dorcas Lester, earned two guineas a week), a lady detective, trained by Mr Johnson (ex-superintendent of police, next door in Oak Tree Road, St John's Wood), married to blind artist **Paul Dene** (Oak Tree Road house; blind after illness). Dog **Toddlekins** (brindle bulldog, rescued after saving a woman from a drunken man in East End). "Council of four": Paul, Dorcas, Mrs Lester, Toddlekins. Mrs Lester is disapproving, "never hold with melodramas." Servant; a respectable clock-winding young man.

Chapter list: I Council of Four; II Helsham Mystery; III Man with the Wild Eyes; IV Secret of the Lake; V Diamond Lizard; VI Prick of a Pin; VII Mysterious Millionaire; VIII Empty House; IX Clothes in the Cupboard; X Haverstock Hill Murder; XI Brown Bear Lamp.

## I. Council of Four
- Dorcas played small parts; last part an old hag. Left theatre when married. Eight years later a solicitor's office (Mr ----, unnamed) reveals her as "Dorcas Dene, the famous lady detective."
- Case: young **Lord Helsham** (Bertie) disappeared; mother Lady Helsham; Dorcas hired.
- Johnson's history: Paul & Dorcas, house in Oak Tree Road; Paul went blind. Dorcas: "Now I'm off! How do you think I look, dear?" Johnson's offer: a case to rescue a blackmailed man (a guinea a day).
- Dorcas meets Saxon in St John's Wood. Paul: "mental vision intensified."
- Dorcas goes to ------ Theatre as gipsy super.

## II. The Helsham Mystery
- Photograph "To dearest Bertie, from Nella": **Nella Dalroy** actress in "The Gipsy Wife"; photographer Alfred Ellis, Baker Street.
- Nella's letter: "he sees no way out... left me all that he has a right to leave me."
- Lord Helsham's mother was a travelling opera singer's daughter? (Late Lord Helsham married a young Scotch lady of travelling opera troupe). Earl killed hunting; posthumous son born premature (a month after father's death).
- Hon. John Farman: uncle, heir if no son.
- Lady Helsham's sister in Dunkeld, Scotland; husband merchant captain who sailed to Australia. Lady's sister's own baby was a girl; swapped (midwife paid). Doctor away.
- Lady Helsham adopted sister's daughter (Nella's real identity? The adopted girl is Nella Dalroy's relative; girl rejected Bertie's marriage). Bertie learned fraud; Lady Helsham had revealed in rage.
- Dorcas stages suicide: placed Bertie's watch and clothes near Cromer. Bertie in hiding at Dunkeld house (Mrs ----, sister). Real Lord Helsham = Bertie's cousin? Result: Lord Helsham the uncle (John Farman) succeeded; Bertie marries Nella in America.
- Paper: "Helsham... 'Times'? 'Mystery cleared up' (Daily Telegraph)."
- Dorcas: "if everybody did the legal thing..."

## III. The Man with the Wild Eyes
- Dorcas gets Saxon involved; "Mr Saxon, the dramatist"; Saxon is "assistant," allowed to write up cases without identifying parties.
- Colonel Hargreaves (Orley Park, near Godalming); daughter **Maud Hargreaves** (25) found in lake, bruised throat and wrists. Story: fainted, fell in.
- Dorcas as trained nurse; Saxon as artist sketching grounds. Inn: "The Chequers."
- Lodge-keeper **Mr Peters**, wife Mrs Peters: stranger "with wild, staring eyes" at gate ~7pm asking name of house.
- Dogs (two big mastiffs). Hobnail boot marks. Woman's small pointed footprints and man's larger ones.
- Dorcas drops purse, finds footprints outside lodge gates (narrow sole, pointed toes). "The man with the wild eyes."

## IV. The Secret of the Lake
- Dorcas's experiment: "Maud!" in dark; Maud says "Victor!"
- Dorcas finds felt hat in reeds on fowl island. Photo of Victor Dubois with erased back, V pin; London Stereoscopic Company, negative 111,492; address Anerley Road, Norwood (Mr Victor Dubois; father Mounseer Dubois, French professor of languages, asylum).
- Maud's story: married secretly Victor Dubois (1891, London) by Dorcas's wire "Yes."
- Victor came from asylum; grabbed Maud by throat; she fell into lake. Victor drowned himself (body found by Dorcas, rowing; then found in lake again, later by "nurse" rowing).
- Inquest: "Victor Dubois, a lunatic, drowned himself."

## V. The Diamond Lizard
- Mrs Charrington (second wife of barrister Mr Charrington); stepson **Claude Charrington** (just left Oxford, going to Bar; pawned watch & chain for £10; acquired banknotes); jewellery missing: diamond and ruby bracelet, diamond and ruby pendant, diamond lizard. Fox-terrier Jack.
- Richmond, "Star and Garter" (waiter **Karl**, manager Mr James). Claude with **Miss Dolamore** (red sailor tie with diamond lizard). Her companion: landlady **Madame Rinaldi** (Carlo Rinaldi Italian husband; 2nd floor Fitzroy Street).
- Bracelet & pendant pawned at Attenborough's (ticket in Claude's name).

## VI. The Prick of a Pin
- Dorcas: The Camorra club, Soho. Saxon uses waiter Guiseppe to get in. Dorcas disguised as stout German frau "Mrs Goldschmidt."
- Rinaldi loses at gambling; Dorcas spills brandy in his pocket; takes pocket-book; pawnticket in Claude's name.
- Mr Charrington replaced jewels; pricked finger on lizard pin; bloodstain on sheet and key. Prior: Rinaldi was a valet who married Charrington's former mistress (Mrs Rinaldi = ex-mistress of Charrington).
- Charrington's story: sent imitation jewels; real ones pawned by Rinaldis. Birthday present; clerk's mistake; Charrington took jewels to jeweller; replaced night while wife asleep. Wife told: "imitation" story.
- Epilogue: Charrington gave Miss Dolamore a true-lovers'-knot; Mrs Charrington's lizard swapped for diamond poodle with ruby eyes.

## VII. The Mysterious Millionaire
- **Judkins Barraclough** (Crœsus of South America; Berkeley Square house; ~45). Wife **Lady Anna Barraclough** (widow of spendthrift first husband who died at 27 of typhoid; brother = Earl of Dashton). Suspects he has a living first wife.
- Bitten right arm (dog story, actually a woman). Left-handed.
- Rose leaves on steps of empty house, No. ---, Burton Crescent. Cabman from St Pancras.
- Dorcas gets keys (two latchkeys) from Lady Anna's dressing-room; slips keys back via letter-box. Dark lantern, goloshes, silent matches.

## VIII. The Empty House
- Indian gentleman "Mr Aleem Mohammed" (dark, white hair, moustache, gold spectacles) bought brandy, saws, indiarubber mats, wire netting.
- Cupboard: ragged female clothes. Back kitchen: tallow trail, chisel, bottles of hydrate of chloral (Poison labels, red), brandy with chloral.
- Caged woman in back first-floor room: wife of Barraclough **Marian Judkins** (drinking herself to death; "Jack" = Judkins). Wedding-ring + diamond ring.
- Dorcas sends Saxon to doctor in Endsleigh Gardens.
- Saxon sees man with white hair at doorway (Aleem).

## IX. The Clothes in the Cupboard
- Inspector **Stromberg** (CID) arrives; Scotland Yard runs Aleem down; Aleem's £5,000 deal.
- Telegram sent to Barraclough "Don't go house. See me at once old place. Important. M." (intercepted). Dorcas's reply "All over. Come Crescent, ten to-night."
- Night sting: Barraclough orders Aleem to strip corpse and dump on doorstep; "she's not dead!" Arrest for attempt to murder Marian Judkins.
- Dorcas: goes to tell Lady Anna she is free.

## X. The Haverstock Hill Murder
- Dorcas away; Oak Tree Road shut; letters to **Mr Jackson, Penton Street, King's Cross** (ex-police-sergeant).
- Inspector **Swanage** (Scotland Yard); Kempton Park; **Flash George** (gambler, fur coat, bet £100 note). Fog.
- Hannaford murder, Haverstock Hill, Jan 5 (maid cry "Murder!"); Mrs Hannaford (widow of **Charles Drayson**, financier who died in Paris Opéra Comique fire); husband Mr Hannaford (stockjobber; confessed quarrel; committed to Broadmoor); his mother (old Mrs Hannaford) engaged Dorcas.
- Flash George seen 2:30am near house. Dorcas disguised as gipsy at Kempton, sold race cards, noted £100 note number ²ₓ❘35421 (Union Bank; from cheque drawn by Drayson, 7 years earlier).

## XI. The Brown Bear Lamp
- Dorcas & Saxon examine house. Front door cracks (warped). Brown bear lamp (purchased by Drayson) moved forward 2–3 inches; hidden slit in bear; hidden banknotes.
- Dorcas plans Hungerford Bridge midnight meeting; Flash George says "Tell him to bring the lot and I'll cash up."
- Organ-grinder disguise; **Thomas Holmes** (Drayson's partner, 5 years penal servitude); old man with grey beard, Inverness cape = **Charles Drayson** (survived Paris fire by faking death, returned to London to recover notes). Drayson jumps into Thames; dies in hospital; confesses. He intended only to stun Mrs Hannaford.
- Mr Hannaford released from Broadmoor; mother's letter. Dorcas: "These are the rewards of my profession." THE END.

Transcriber's notes: underscores mark italics.
